findings.obligation: The acceptance designer owns every test; the implementation author adds a test only where the recorded oracle cannot go green without it, and never beyond the recorded oracle (nw-code-craftsmanship rule 35; nw-sc-review-dimensions, Producer-Authored Tests). The recorded oracle for S1 is tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs with supports crates/openlore-review-app/Cargo.toml and the two files under tests/acceptance/support/review_app/; the only in-crate locator acceptance.md records is crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs::a_purge_between_scan_start_and_plan_write_leaves_no_rows.

findings.obligation: A rule the code checks at runtime, or only in a test, that the types could make impossible is a finding (nw-type-level-design, 'Decide before writing' 4 and 'Write' 3; nw-certainty-by-construction).
findings.observation: Open and unchanged by the delta; retained as non-blocking. Resume still models a four-way partition of the plan's positions as four parallel public collections, to_read, carried, already_read and skipped, the fourth added by this feature. Nothing in the type stops one position appearing in two of them; the disjointness the count depends on is asserted only by property tests. Resume::kept at resume.rs:104-125 already rebuilds the per-position-with-disposition sequence the type could carry, and the revised oracle binding now consumes exactly that sequence (sut_picked_up reads verdict.kept()), so the shape the type is missing is the one the oracle already reads. The owner states that reshaping Resume would disturb that binding; the remediation below keeps kept(), to_read, carried, already_read and skipped as public observations, so the binding and tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs:402 are unaffected.
findings.remediation: Carry the verdict as one sequence of positions each with its disposition - the KeptRow shape already introduced, extended with the carried-skip reason - and derive to_read, carried, already_read, skipped and kept() over it, so no two of them can name the same position and every current reader keeps its surface. Not required for this feature; schedule it with the next change to the resume verdict.

The two EXAMINE-gap journeys are sound and add no finding. Both are oracle-owned additions to the recorded oracle path and its declared supports; no production file and no existing test changed, and no assertion, case or input anywhere was narrowed. The fault they drive is real, not a fixture that could pass vacuously: REFUSE_MARK_REPO_READ is the string 'refuse_mark_repo_read', which crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:314 already parses into TestFault::RefuseMarkRepoRead, and config.rs:311-320 returns an error for an unknown value, so a mistyped token would stop the app at startup rather than silently inject nothing; the same seam is the one review_app_scan_store_failure already drives. a_run_cut_short_keeps_what_it_saved_and_the_run_after_it_reads_only_the_rest observes E2 through the real HTTP port: it asserts the picked-up run ends 'interrupted' and the last one 'completed', that nothing her scan had already saved is read again by either later run, that the runs read exactly her three chosen repos, and that the queue carries one repos-read line saying three; under a resume-only count the finishing run read two, so the scenario fails on the behaviour it names. repos_her_scan_had_to_read_again_are_counted_once_each observes E5 and E6 over four runs with the fault switched on, off, on and off: it asserts as part of the scenario that at least two different repos were read by more than one run, so it cannot pass vacuously if the seam stops producing re-reads, and then that the count is still three rather than the number of reads. Every expected value in both is anchored to PRIYA_CHOICE_OF_THREE and to the repos the GitHub double was actually asked for, never to production output, so neither is circular. show_one_paused_scan's per-test static AtomicBool is a one-shot print guard for --nocapture diagnostics; it is swapped atomically and no assertion reads it, so it adds no shared mutable state an assertion depends on. The two added support steps restart the real binary on the same store and keep the ReviewWorld move explicit; the third returns the status and the repos read, as the existing steps do.

diagnostic: Accepted at HEAD 3ab2dd1. The delta is oracle-only and strengthens coverage; the two non-blocking implementation findings are unaffected and stay open. git diff --name-only 7eb6adb HEAD lists .nwave/examine.json, scripts/examine/review-app-oracle, the oracle file, the two acceptance support files and the feature docs and run records. No file under crates/ changed, so R4 (review-domain, adapter-review-store, ports: 263 passed) and R15 (cargo xtask check-arch: OK over 30 workspace members) stand on unchanged inputs and were not repeated. Re-executed, all exit 0: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture, 9 passed; cargo clippy -p openlore-review-app --all-targets -- -D warnings, no warning; cargo test -p openlore-review-app, 320 passed over 22 binaries, review_app_scan_store_failure among them. The two journeys close the EXAMINE gaps at the right owner and through the real HTTP port. The interrupted-run journey asserts the picked-up run ends interrupted and the last completed, that nothing already saved is read again, that the runs read exactly her three chosen repos and that the queue says three; under a resume-only count the finishing run read two, so it fails on the behaviour it names. The re-read journey switches the fault on, off, on and off over four runs and asserts, as part of the scenario, that at least two different repos were read by more than one run before claiming the count is three, so it cannot pass vacuously. The seam is real rather than a fixture: 'refuse_mark_repo_read' is already parsed at crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:314 and an unknown token is refused at startup. Every expected value is anchored to PRIYA_CHOICE_OF_THREE and to the repos the GitHub double was asked for, so neither journey is circular, and no existing assertion, case or input was narrowed anywhere in the delta. Open, non-blocking, owner implementation, both unchanged by this delta and both in production files this delta does not touch: the two producer-authored proptests outside the recorded oracle, whose justification lapsed once the oracle covered L1 and whose L4 obligations acceptance.md already records, kept by the owner's decision; and Resume still modelling a four-way partition as four parallel collections, so the disjointness the count rests on is representable as broken. Limitations retained: typesafe unavailable, exit 3, key absent from this process, so no service judgment is claimed; this repository has no test-impact selector, so selection stayed mechanical from the touched paths; no timing statement is made, no half-budget or derogation case arose; native peer messaging exposed no owner session to address, so the two open findings travel to their owner through the root.
